report.objective: Say precisely what it would take to bring failover readiness into the Java product, and what is genuinely close versus what only looks close. Three read-only assessment modules exist in the earlier Python line with 52 passing tests, and the Java product has no failover code at all. The Product Owner believes this work is near ready. This movement replaces that belief with a map: which parts could ship without a single open decision being answered, which parts are blocked and by exactly which decision, and what the port would actually cost. It writes one document and no code.
output_contract: A truthful answer to whether failover is close, and to what exactly would have to happen first.

recommended_reasoning.reason: A cross-line architecture question whose main hazard is producing a confident plan over unanswered decisions.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Every command runs from the repository root.
Run only the commands named above. This is a reading and writing task; build nothing.
Run `git diff --check origin/main` before committing and fix what it names.
Leave the worktree clean: write reports outside the repository or remove them before closing.
A mechanical mismatch between this packet and the code is settled against the code and named in the SESSION_CLOSE; a RELAY_QUESTION is only for a decision in conflict.
No emoji, no tool-identifying footer, no external URL in commits, the pull request or code comments.
Commit early and often on your lane.
The SESSION_CLOSE answers in one sentence how much could ship before any open decision is answered, and names the decision that blocks the most.
risks: Producing an implementation plan that quietly assumes the open decisions will go a particular way, which is how an assumption becomes a contract.
Filling a vendor semantic from general model knowledge because the gap is inconvenient.
Reading the 52 passing tests as evidence of readiness for the Java product; they prove the Python derivation, not that the facts it needs can be produced here.
Recommending that an invariant be relaxed as though that were an engineering decision rather than a Product Owner one.

in: Read the three modules and the architecture document, and describe what the Python line actually computes today -- the inputs it needs, the verdict vocabulary it may emit, and the stop-conditions it maps. Describe behaviour, not file structure.

For each capability it provides, state whether it could be brought into the Java product with no open decision answered, or name the exact decision id that blocks it. A capability blocked by a decision that needs real-device evidence must say so, because that evidence does not exist for any feature yet.

Identify what the Java product would have to gain for the unblocked part to work: which existing collectors already produce the facts, which facts have no producer, and where a readiness surface would sit in the frozen information architecture.

State plainly what is close and what is not. If the honest answer is that little can ship before the open decisions and the first real-device run, say that in those words rather than producing a plan that depends on them.

Respect the invariants as boundaries of the analysis, not obstacles to route around: readiness is not authorization, the assessment may not emit a proceed verdict, and no plan, executor or vendor adapter belongs in the assessment layer. If the analysis suggests any of these should change, say so as a recommendation to the Product Owner and never as a design.
Write it to docs/design/FAILOVER_READINESS_IN_THE_JAVA_PRODUCT_2026_09_15.md with a status line of DRAFT -- ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS. NOT AUTHORITY, NOT A CONTRACT.
out: Writing any Java, Python, TypeScript, SQL or test. This movement writes exactly one document.

Designing or proposing a failover execution path, a plan compiler, an executor or a vendor adapter. The assessment layer is read-only by test-enforced invariant and this analysis does not prepare its removal.
Answering, pre-empting or assuming any open decision. Name it, say what it blocks, and stop.
Inferring a vendor semantic that a decision records as unknown. The vendor-semantics law forbids filling that gap from general knowledge and this document must not.
Any change to project/*.json, to the backlog, or to any contract.
